Galician

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈas/ [ˈas̺]
  • Rhymes: -as
  • Hyphenation: ás

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

ás f pl

  1. plural of á

Etymology 2

[edit]

From contraction of preposition a (“to, towards”) + feminine plural definite article as (“the”).

Contraction

[edit]

ás f pl (masculine sg ao, feminine sg á, masculine plural aos)

  1. to the, towards the

Further reading

[edit]
  • “o”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “ás”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

Icelandic

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /auːs/
  • Rhymes: -auːs

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Norse áss, from Proto-Germanic *ansaz.

Noun

[edit]

ás m (genitive singular áss, nominative plural ásar)

  1. beam, rafter, pole
  2. axis
Declension
[edit]
Declension of ás (masculine)
singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative ás ásinn ásar ásarnir
accusative ás ásinn ása ásana
dative ás, ási ásnum ásum ásunum
genitive áss ássins ása ásanna

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Old Norse áss, likely from Proto-Germanic *amsaz, cognate with Gothic 𐌰𐌼𐍃 (ams, “shoulder”), but possibly the same as ás (1).

Noun

[edit]

ás m (genitive singular áss, nominative plural ásar)

  1. long low hill, (low) ridge
Declension
[edit]
Declension of ás (masculine)
singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative ás ásinn ásar ásarnir
accusative ás ásinn ása ásana
dative ás, ási ásnum ásum ásunum
genitive áss ássins ása ásanna

Etymology 3

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin ās, perhaps via Middle Low German [Term?].

Noun

[edit]

ás m (genitive singular áss, nominative plural ásar)

  1. pip (one of the spots on a die)
  2. the side of a die that has only one pip
  3. ace (playing card)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of ás (masculine)
singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative ás ásinn ásar ásarnir
accusative ás ásinn ása ásana
dative ás, ási ásnum ásum ásunum
genitive áss ássins ása ásanna

Etymology 4

[edit]

From Old Norse áss, ǫ́ss, from Proto-Germanic *ansuz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énsus, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ens- (“to engender, beget”).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • Ás

Noun

[edit]

ás m (genitive singular áss, nominative plural æsir)

  1. one of the Æsir, the principal Norse gods
Declension
[edit]
Declension of ás (masculine)

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈa(j)s/ [ˈa(ɪ̯)s]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈa(j)s/ [ˈa(ɪ̯)s]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈa(j)ʃ/ [ˈa(ɪ̯)ʃ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈaʃ/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: (Brazil) -as, (Portugal, Rio de Janeiro) -aʃ, (Brazil) -ajs, (Rio de Janeiro) -ajʃ
  • Homophones: hás, às, as (Brazil)
  • Hyphenation: ás

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin as (“a type of Roman coin”).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • az (obsolete)

Noun

[edit]

ás m (plural ases)

  1. (card games) ace (card with a single spot)
  2. ace (an expert at something)
    Synonyms: especialista, expert
  3. (military aviation) ace (pilot who shot down five or more enemy aircraft)
